rows.location: course/modules/AP/AP1/L07.html line 113: "the bias is all in the variance: the sample variance bound of Lesson 5 is biased upward, and so is the square of the sample maximum Sharpe ratio it equals"
rows.evidence: Round-1 fix applied to the Sharpe ratio, but the same defect remains in the clause before it. Lesson 5 (L05.html line 227 and Theorem 2.4) defines the variance bound as sigma(m)/E[m], a ratio of standard deviations, e.g. "the variance bound is sigma(x*)/E[x*] = 0.116052". Theorem 3.3 with a pinned mean 1/R_f gives E[Var_T(x-hat*)] >= Var(x*), i.e. upward bias of the SQUARED bound; sqrt is concave, so E[sigma-hat] >= sigma does not follow. The sentence now says "the sample variance bound ... is biased upward, and so is the square of the ... Sharpe ratio it equals", which is internally inconsistent: the bound equals the Sharpe ratio, so one cannot be biased unsquared and the other only squared.
rows.fix: Change to "the square of the sample variance bound of Lesson 5 is biased upward, and so is the square of the sample maximum Sharpe ratio it equals" (or "the sample variance of x-hat* is biased upward, and so is the squared bound and the squared maximum Sharpe ratio").

rows.location: course/modules/AP/AP1/L07.html canon-breaks item 2 (line 285): "if p_t = E_t[m x_{t+1}], the tower property gives E[z_t p_t] = E[m z_t x_{t+1}], so z_t x_{t+1} is a payoff with price z_t p_t that every conditional SDF also prices unconditionally"
rows.evidence: The claim is now derived on the page instead of asserted, which answers round 1. Re-derived: E[z_t p_t] = E[z_t E_t[m x_{t+1}]] = E[E_t[z_t m x_{t+1}]] = E[m z_t x_{t+1}], using z_t measurable at t (stated: "known at the start of the month"). The step "pull z_t inside E_t and take expectations" needs z_t m x_{t+1} integrable (e.g. z_t bounded, or E|z_t m x_{t+1}| < inf); otherwise E[z_t p_t] may not exist. The passage states no such assumption, and BLUEPRINT/VERIFIER 2.4 require complete assumptions. Minor second point: the derivation writes m without a time index while Lesson 4 line 370 writes the same relation as p_t = E_t[m_{t+1} x_{t+1}]; not a registry collision (m is a local symbol per notation.json "about"), but inconsistent across lessons.
rows.fix: Insert the assumption: "Multiplying payoffs by a bounded signal z_t known at the start of the month (or any z_t with E|z_t m x_{t+1}| < inf) ..." and write m_{t+1} as in Lesson 4.
